<!-- Generated by tools/cli-reference.py from `backdown serve --help`. Edit the help in crates/backdown-cli (or the notes in the script) and run it again. -->


```text
backdown serve [OPTIONS]
```

## Options

`--port <PORT>`
: Port to listen on. Default: `8787`.

`--host <HOST>`
: Also listen on this address (e.g. this computer's Tailscale IP) so other devices can look; from there BackDown only shows, and changes need this computer. 127.0.0.1 always listens. Default: `127.0.0.1`.

`--no-open`
: Don't open a browser, just print the link.

Also takes the [global options](/docs/cli/#global-options) `--db` and `--local`.

## Good to know

The browser listens on 127.0.0.1 and prints a private link with a one-time token. It only reads: copying, wiping, rescues and rescans need the background service (`backdown app`, or `backdown service install` then `backdown open`). `--host ADDRESS` also listens on that address, a Tailscale address such as 100.x.y.z say, and prints the link to use from your other devices. From anywhere but this computer, BackDown only shows what's there: nothing can be wiped, copied, rescued, mounted, opened or changed, and the link's token is still needed. A wildcard such as 0.0.0.0 listens on every address, 127.0.0.1 included.

## Examples

```sh
backdown serve
# another port, and just print the link
backdown serve --port 8788 --no-open
# also look from your other devices, at this computer's Tailscale address
backdown serve --host 100.x.y.z
```
